cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; carry lira for minibuses, village cafés and tea gardens. Tip 5 to 10 percent.
name: Trabzon
tagline: Cliff monastery, tea hills and the green Black Sea
summary: Trabzon is the gateway to Türkiye's lush Black Sea coast. See the Sümela Monastery clinging to a cliff in a misty forest, the frescoed Hagia Sophia of Trabzon, and Atatürk's mansion, then head into the Kaçkar mountains to Uzungöl lake, the tea terraces of Rize and the highland villages of Ayder.
seasonNote: Summer is mild and green; rain falls all year, and highland roads may close in winter.
arrival: Trabzon Airport has flights from Istanbul (about 2 hours) and Ankara.
gettingAround: Dolmuş minibuses in town; tours or a car for Sümela and Uzungöl.
foodTip: Hamsi (Black Sea anchovies), kuymak cheese fondue, Akçaabat köfte, Laz böreği and fresh Rize tea.
buyTip: Rize tea, hazelnuts and Trabzon silver filigree (hasır bilezik).

items.name: Sümela Monastery
items.summary: Greek Orthodox monastery built into a sheer cliff high above a forested valley.
items.tip: Go early; a lift or path takes you up.

items.name: Hagia Sophia of Trabzon
items.summary: 13th-century Byzantine church with frescoes, now a mosque.
items.tip: Look at the carved Genesis frieze on the south porch.

items.name: Atatürk Mansion
items.summary: White hillside villa where Atatürk stayed, with gardens and city views.

items.name: Boztepe Hill
items.summary: Hill with tea gardens overlooking the city and the Black Sea.
items.tip: Have tea and simit at sunset.

items.name: Uzungöl
items.summary: Lake in a mountain valley with a mosque by the water and wooden chalets.
items.tip: Walk up to the viewpoints above the lake.

items.name: Ayder plateau
items.summary: Highland village of wooden houses, waterfalls and hot springs.
items.tip: Stay overnight; try the hot spring.

items.name: Rize tea terraces
items.summary: Tea plantations covering the hills, with a tea garden overlooking the town.
items.tip: Visit the Tea Research Institute garden.

items.name: Hamsi
items.summary: Black Sea anchovies, fried in cornmeal or baked with rice.

items.name: Kuymak
items.summary: Melted cheese, butter and cornmeal, eaten with bread for breakfast.
items.tip: Have it with a Black Sea breakfast spread.

items.name: Akçaabat köfte
items.summary: Grilled meatballs from Akçaabat, served with peppers and bread.

cashTip: Cards are widely accepted; tip about 10 percent if service is not included.
name: Paphos
summary: Paphos is a UNESCO town in western Cyprus, full of Roman floor mosaics and royal tombs carved from rock. See the mosaics of the House of Dionysos, explore the Tombs of the Kings, swim at Aphrodite's Rock where the goddess rose from the sea, and drive to the wild Akamas peninsula and the Avakas Gorge.
seasonNote: Swimming from May to November; July and August are very hot.
arrival: Paphos Airport is 20 minutes away; Larnaca is 1h30 by shuttle.
gettingAround: Buses link Kato Paphos and the old town; rent a car for Akamas and the mountains (drive on the left).
foodTip: Halloumi, souvla, kleftiko, meze and Commandaria sweet wine.
buyTip: Halloumi, Lefkara lace and Commandaria wine.

items.name: Paphos Archaeological Park
items.summary: Roman villas with some of the finest floor mosaics in the world.
items.tip: Start at the House of Dionysos.

items.name: Tombs of the Kings
items.summary: Underground Hellenistic tombs carved from rock with Doric columns.

items.name: Aphrodite's Rock (Petra tou Romiou)
items.summary: Sea stack where Aphrodite was said to rise from the waves.
items.tip: Swim around the rock for eternal youth (legend says).

items.name: Paphos Harbour and Castle
items.summary: Harbour promenade with a small medieval fort.

items.name: Avakas Gorge
items.summary: Narrow limestone gorge with a walk through towering walls.

items.name: Akamas and the Blue Lagoon
items.summary: Wild peninsula with turquoise Blue Lagoon reached by boat or jeep.

items.name: Kykkos Monastery
items.summary: Richly decorated mountain monastery in the Troodos.

items.name: Cypriot meze
items.summary: A long parade of small dishes, from dips to grilled meats.

items.name: Kleftiko
items.summary: Lamb slow-baked in a sealed clay oven.

items.name: Halloumi and souvla
items.summary: Grilled halloumi and big chunks of meat on the spit.

cashTip: Cards and IC cards work in most places, but carry cash for small restaurants, shrines and rural buses. No tipping.
name: Naoshima
tagline: Art island of the Seto Inland Sea
summary: Naoshima is a small island turned into a world of contemporary art. See Monet's Water Lilies in Tadao Ando's underground Chichu Art Museum, the yellow pumpkin by Yayoi Kusama on the pier, the Art House Project inside old village houses, and bathe in the art bathhouse I♥湯, then hop to Teshima for its teardrop art museum.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best; the Setouchi Triennale draws crowds in festival years; most museums close on Mondays.
arrival: Ferries from Uno port (1 hour from Okayama by train) take 20 minutes, or from Takamatsu 50 minutes.
gettingAround: Rent a bike or e-bike; island buses link the port, Honmura and Benesse.
foodTip: Seto Inland Sea seafood and sanuki udon on the way via Takamatsu.

connections.note: Shinkansen to Okayama, train to Uno, ferry.
Shinkansen to Okayama, train to Uno, ferry.
Shinkansen to Okayama, train to Uno, ferry.

items.name: Chichu Art Museum
items.summary: Tadao Ando's underground museum lit by daylight, with Monet, Turrell and De Maria.
items.expect: Timed tickets; closed Mondays; no photos.
items.tip: Book weeks ahead in high season.

items.name: Yellow Pumpkin
items.summary: Kusama's dotted yellow pumpkin on a pier, the island's symbol.

items.name: Benesse House Museum
items.summary: Museum-hotel by the sea with works placed indoors and on the beach.
items.tip: Walk the outdoor art along the coast.

items.name: Art House Project
items.summary: Old houses, a temple and a shrine in Honmura turned into art installations.

items.name: Lee Ufan Museum
items.summary: Quiet Ando building holding Lee Ufan's minimal stone and steel works.

items.name: Naoshima Bath I♥湯
items.summary: Working public bathhouse designed as an artwork by Shinro Ohtake.
items.tip: End the day with a soak.

items.name: Teshima Art Museum
items.summary: A concrete shell like a water drop where water beads across the floor.

items.name: Island cafés in Honmura
items.summary: Small cafés in old houses serving curry, rice sets and coffee.

items.name: Inland Sea seafood
items.summary: Fresh fish and seafood bowls near the port.

items.name: Sanuki udon in Takamatsu
items.summary: Thick chewy udon from Kagawa, cheap and fast at self-service shops.
items.tip: Order kake udon and add tempura.

cashTip: Cards and IC cards work in most places, but carry cash for small restaurants, shrines and rural buses. No tipping.
name: Matsumoto
tagline: The black crow castle and the Japan Alps
summary: Matsumoto is a mountain city with one of Japan's few original castles, the black Matsumoto Castle. Climb its steep wooden stairs, walk the old merchant street of Nakamachi, see Yayoi Kusama's hometown art museum, and use the city as a gateway to Kamikochi's alpine valley and the Northern Alps.
seasonNote: Cherry blossom in mid-April; Kamikochi is open mid-April to mid-November.
arrival: Limited express Azusa trains from Tokyo Shinjuku take 2h40; from Nagoya the Shinano takes 2 hours.
gettingAround: Walk or use the town loop bus and free bikes; buses to Kamikochi.
foodTip: Shinshu soba, basashi (horse sashimi), sanzoku-yaki fried chicken and apples.
buyTip: Matsumoto temari balls and wooden furniture.

items.name: Matsumoto Castle
items.summary: Black wooden castle of 1594, one of Japan's 12 original keeps.
items.tip: Photograph it reflected in the moat with the Alps behind.

items.name: Nakamachi Street
items.summary: Merchant street of white and black namako-walled storehouses.

items.name: Matsumoto City Museum of Art
items.summary: Museum with a large collection by hometown artist Yayoi Kusama.

items.name: Nawate Street
items.summary: Riverside lane of frog-themed shops and snacks by the Metoba River.

items.name: Kaichi School
items.summary: Western-style 1876 schoolhouse, one of Japan's oldest.
items.expect: Check it is open after renovation.

items.name: Kamikochi
items.summary: Car-free alpine valley of clear rivers, Kappa Bridge and jagged peaks.
items.expect: Mid-April to mid-November only; bus from Matsumoto.
items.tip: Walk from Taisho Pond to Kappa Bridge and Myojin.

items.name: Daio Wasabi Farm
items.summary: Huge wasabi farm with clear streams and water wheels.

items.name: Shinshu soba
items.summary: Buckwheat noodles from Nagano, served cold with dipping sauce.

items.name: Sanzoku-yaki
items.summary: Large fried chicken thigh marinated in garlic, a Matsumoto speciality.

items.name: Basashi
items.summary: Horse sashimi, a Nagano speciality served with ginger and soy.
items.tip: Try a small plate at an izakaya.

cashTip: Carry cash for night markets and small eateries; EasyCard works on buses and in convenience stores. No tipping.
name: Hualien
tagline: Marble gorges of Taroko and the Pacific coast
summary: Hualien is the gateway to Taroko Gorge, where a river has cut through marble mountains on Taiwan's wild east coast. Walk the gorge trails, see the Qingshui Cliffs dropping into the Pacific, cycle the coast, and eat your way through Dongdamen night market. Check trail status first: parts of Taroko were damaged in the April 2024 earthquake and reopen in stages.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best; typhoons can hit from July to October.
arrival: Trains from Taipei take 2 to 3 hours; book seats ahead on weekends.
gettingAround: Scooter, taxi or tour for Taroko; buses are infrequent.
foodTip: Bian shi wontons, mochi, Indigenous Amis dishes and night-market snacks.
baseArea: Near Hualien station or the city centre

connections.note: Puyuma and Taroko express trains; book ahead.

items.name: Taroko Gorge
items.summary: Marble canyon of sheer cliffs, temples and trails above a turquoise river.
items.expect: Some trails remain closed after the 2024 earthquake; check the park website.
items.tip: Start at the visitor centre and the Shakadang Trail if open.

items.name: Qingshui Cliffs
items.summary: Cliffs falling straight into the deep blue Pacific.

items.name: Qixingtan Beach
items.summary: Crescent pebble beach with a bike path and mountain backdrop.
items.expect: Pebbles, strong surf; not for swimming.
items.tip: Cycle the coastal path from the city.

items.name: East Rift Valley and coast
items.summary: Coastal drive past Shitiping rocks and the Tropic of Cancer marker.
items.tip: Stop at Shitiping and the Baxian caves.

items.name: Pine Garden
items.summary: Japanese-era command post in pines overlooking the port, now an art space.

items.name: Dongdamen Night Market
items.summary: Big night market with Indigenous grilled meats, seafood and snacks.

items.name: Bian shi wontons
items.summary: Hualien's famous wonton soup, served at long-running shops.
items.tip: Order a bowl with the clear broth.

items.name: Hualien mochi
items.summary: Soft rice cakes with sesame, peanut or red bean fillings.
items.tip: Buy fresh ones to eat that day.

cashTip: Mobile payment (Alipay, WeChat Pay) is everywhere and both accept foreign cards; carry some cash too. No tipping.
name: Lijiang
tagline: Naxi old town under Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
summary: Lijiang's UNESCO old town is a maze of canals, stone bridges and wooden Naxi houses under the glacier-capped Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. Ride the cable car toward the glacier, see the Black Dragon Pool reflection, stay in quieter Baisha and Shuhe villages, and hike the Tiger Leaping Gorge, one of the world's deepest.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are clear; July and August are rainy and busy with domestic tourists.
arrival: Flights from Kunming, Chengdu and Shanghai; high-speed trains from Kunming take about 3 hours.
gettingAround: Walk the old town; taxis and DiDi for villages; buses to Tiger Leaping Gorge.
foodTip: Naxi baba flatbread, yak hot pot, black dragon pool fish and Yunnan mushrooms.
buyTip: Pu'er tea and Naxi Dongba crafts.

items.name: Dayan Old Town
items.summary: UNESCO town of canals, stone bridges and Naxi wooden houses.
items.expect: Very commercial in the centre; old-town maintenance fee may apply.
items.tip: Climb Lion Hill for the rooftop view; explore early morning.

items.name: Black Dragon Pool
items.summary: Pool reflecting a marble bridge, a pavilion and the snow mountain.
items.tip: Go at sunrise for the mountain reflection.

items.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
items.summary: Glacier mountain with a cable car to 4,500 m and Blue Moon Valley lakes.
items.tip: Book cable car tickets ahead; carry oxygen.

items.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge
items.summary: Deep gorge of the Jinsha River with a famous high trail.
items.expect: Two-day trek or day viewpoint; landslide risk in rain.
items.tip: Walk the high trail with a night at a guesthouse.

items.name: Baisha village
items.summary: Old Naxi village with Ming-dynasty murals and quiet lanes.

items.name: Shuhe Old Town
items.summary: Smaller old town with streams and a slower pace.
items.tip: Stay here for a quieter base.

items.name: Mu Residence
items.summary: Palace of the Naxi chieftains, nicknamed Lijiang's Forbidden City.
items.tip: Climb behind it to the Wangu Tower view.

items.name: Naxi baba
items.summary: Layered fried flatbread, sweet or savoury.

items.name: Yak hot pot
items.summary: Hot pot with yak meat and mountain mushrooms.

items.name: Yunnan rice noodles
items.summary: Rice noodles cooked at the table in a hot broth.

cashTip: Cash is king; carry kip, and US dollars for some tours. Tipping is not expected but welcome.
name: Vang Vieng
tagline: Karst peaks, lagoons and river adventures
summary: Vang Vieng sits among dramatic limestone karsts on the Nam Song river. Now calmer and more outdoorsy than in its party years, it's a place for hot-air balloon rides at sunrise, swimming in the Blue Lagoons, exploring caves, kayaking and tubing, and climbing Nam Xay viewpoint.
seasonNote: November to February is dry and clear; March to May is smoky from field burning; June to October is rainy.
arrival: The Laos-China Railway reaches Vang Vieng in 1 hour from Vientiane and 1 hour from Luang Prabang.
gettingAround: Rent a scooter, bike or buggy; tuk-tuks to the lagoons.
foodTip: Laap, sticky rice, khao piak sen noodle soup and Beerlao.

items.name: Hot-air balloon at sunrise
items.summary: Balloon over the karsts and river at dawn.

items.name: Blue Lagoon 1 and Tham Phu Kham
items.summary: Turquoise swimming lagoon below a cave with a reclining Buddha.
items.tip: Climb to the cave first, then swim.

items.name: Nam Xay viewpoint
items.summary: Steep scramble to a peak with a motorbike prop and a sweeping karst view.
items.expect: Steep and rocky; 30 to 45 minutes up.
items.tip: Go for sunrise or late afternoon.

items.name: Nam Song kayaking and tubing
items.summary: Paddle or float down the river past karsts.
items.expect: Life jackets; avoid high water in rainy season.
items.tip: Combine with Tham Nam water cave.

items.name: Tham Chang cave
items.summary: Cave once used as a refuge, with a spring-fed pool and views.
items.tip: Cross the bridge south of town.

items.name: Laap and sticky rice
items.summary: Minced meat salad with herbs, lime and roasted rice, with sticky rice.

items.name: Khao piak sen
items.summary: Thick rice noodle soup with chicken, a Lao breakfast.

items.name: Riverside sunset Beerlao
items.summary: Riverside bars facing the karsts at sunset.
items.tip: Pick a deck with a view.
